name: Lamb potjiekos
summary: Lamb, potatoes and vegetables layered in a three-legged cast-iron pot and cooked slowly over the coals, unstirred, until everything is tender in its own gravy.
about: Potjiekos (pot food) goes back to the cast-iron pots carried by trekkers and hunters, kept simmering over the fire. Today a potjie is the weekend fireside meal: the meat goes in first, the vegetables are layered on top, the lid stays on, and friends gather round the fire while it cooks. A No. 3 pot feeds a family of six.
steps: Make a fire and let it burn down to medium coals, then set a No. 3 potjie over them and heat the oil until shimmering, about 5 minutes.
Brown the lamb in two batches, about 5 minutes a batch, until well coloured all over. Return all the meat to the pot.
Add the onions and fry with the meat, stirring, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, paprika, coriander, rosemary and bay leaves for 1 minute.

Pour in 1 cup of the stock, put the lid on and rake the coals so the pot just simmers gently. Cook for 1 hour 15 minutes, checking every 20 minutes and adding a splash of stock if the bottom looks dry, until the lamb is nearly tender.

Season the meat with half the salt. Layer the vegetables on top of the lamb without stirring: potatoes first, then carrots, then butternut, then green beans and mushrooms. Season the top with the rest of the salt and some pepper.
Whisk the tomato paste and chutney into the remaining stock and pour it over the vegetables. Put the lid back on.

Simmer gently for 1 hour without stirring, adding a few fresh coals under the pot every 20 minutes to keep a slow bubble. It is ready when a knife slides easily into the potatoes and the lamb pulls away from the bone.
Take the pot off the coals and serve at the fire straight from the pot, spooning down through the layers so everyone gets meat, vegetables and gravy. Rice or pap goes alongside.
